chunks: Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Muzaffar al-Alawi (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud al-Ayyashi told us, from his father, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Walid told us, from Abbas ibn Hilal, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

He mentioned: That the name of Iblees is "Al-Harith", and indeed Allah, Exalted and Glorious, says: "O Iblees" meaning O disobedient. He was named Iblees because he despaired from the mercy of Allah, Exalted and Glorious.

key_terms.الْحَارِث: Al-Harith, the proper name of Iblees

ai.seo_question: What is the actual name of Iblees and why is he called Iblees?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'Al-Harith' is Iblees's proper name, while 'Iblees' is a descriptive title derived from the root meaning despair, signifying his exclusion from Allah's mercy. This narration highlights the linguistic nuance in Quranic address, where 'O Iblees' is interpreted as 'O the disobedient one,' emphasizing his state of defiance rather than serving as a personal name. This explanation aligns with Shia exegetical traditions that distinguish between proper names and honorific or descriptive titles used in divine discourse.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Mudaffar bin Ja’far bin Mudaffar al-Alawi, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Ja’far bin Muhammed bin Mas’ud al-‘Ayyashi, from his father, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Waleed, from Abbas bin Hilal, from Abu’l-Hasan al-Rida, peace be upon him,

that he mentioned: The name of Iblees is Harith, and Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, only says: «O Iblees» [15:32] as in: O disobedient. He was named Iblees [1] because he despaired from the mercy of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He.
